title: A Harbor for the Postcard
premise: Elodie Okafor built her career orchestrating other people's perfect days after her own engagement collapsed, and she no longer believes in the vows she sells. When a snowstorm strands her on Harrow Island with Julian Ashe — the rival planner whose ambition once cost them both everything, including a night in their twenties neither has admitted to — she is forced to plan one last wedding alongside the man she swore to outshine. As thaw approaches and the last ferry of the season nears, Elodie must choose between the partnership that would save her company and the love that finally makes her honest. She lets the ferry leave without her.
about_author: Mara Vane is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade behind the scenes of other people's happily-ever-afters before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town much like Harrow Island, where the ferries keep their own unforgiving schedule.

chapters.title: The Vow Vendor
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At a lavish Boston wedding she directs with flawless detachment, a bride asks if Elodie believes in marriage; her evasive answer reveals the wound beneath her professionalism. Emotional beat: competent armor cracking at the seams.

chapters.title: Ashe & Okafor
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A merger offer arrives: rival firm Ashe Events wants to acquire hers, with Julian Ashe himself leading negotiations. Their boardroom sparring crackles with old history. Beat: rivalry as intimacy in disguise.

chapters.title: The Harrow Job
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian accepts a destination wedding on remote Harrow Island partly to force proximity with Elodie, telling himself it's strategy. He requests her by name for the contract. Beat: self-deception established.

chapters.title: Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The ferry to Harrow carries Elodie, Julian, and a wedding party of strangers; their bickering masks awareness of each other. Weather warnings begin. Beat: the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. The storm hits early; roads close, power flickers, and the wedding is postponed indefinitely. Stranded together in the island inn, they share whiskey and an almost-confession. Beat: forced honesty begins.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A blackout and a bottle of the innkeeper's blackcurrant liqueur lead to the night in their twenties finally surfacing — the kiss they never spoke of, the opportunity Julian chose over her. Beat: the past made present.

chapters.title: What Ambition Costs
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian admits he took the promotion that ended their first almost-romance because he believed love was a liability to his rise. He watches Elodie sleep and understands what he traded. Beat: guilt made articulate.

chapters.title: Plan B Wedding
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. With vendors unreachable, the stranded pair must build the wedding from scratch — island fishermen, the inn's kitchen, candlelight. Working together rekindles their old creative chemistry. Beat: collaboration as courtship.

chapters.title: The Bride Who Waited
chapters.summary: Bride Priya's POV (interlude). Priya confides she delayed the wedding on purpose, sensing her fiancé's hesitation, and asks Elodie whether love or timing should win. Her question lands like a mirror. Beat: theme voiced by an outsider.

chapters.title: Terms of the Merger
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian's business partner calls: the acquisition will only proceed if Elodie signs away her name and creative control. Julian hides the clause. Beat: corruption of power beginning its quiet work.

chapters.title: Thaw Lines
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Storm lifts partially; Elodie finds the contract addendum in Julian's bag. Confrontation on the frozen dock — she accuses him of repeating his oldest sin. Beat: trust shattered at the exact moment it bloomed.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Innkeeper Maren's POV (interlude). Maren, widowed young, tells Elodie about the last ferry of the season and the husband who never got on it. Belonging, she says, is a place you decide, not a place you're assigned. Beat: wisdom offered without preaching.

chapters.title: Cold Openings
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian renegotiates alone, gutting the exploitative clause at the cost of his partner's fury and possibly his firm. He does it without telling Elodie, unsure if redemption requires witness. Beat: sacrifice in secret.

chapters.title: The Wedding, At Last
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The improvised wedding happens under a clearing sky — imperfect, handmade, alive. Watching Priya's vows, Elodie feels something she thought was dead stir. Beat: belief returning through someone else's joy.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Dual POV. That night Julian tries to tell Elodie what he did; she, braced for betrayal again, cuts him off and announces she's taking the first boat out. Both retreat wounded. Beat: miscommunication at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Departures Board
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The ferry returns early; Elodie packs, signs nothing, and stands at the dock. Julian doesn't come to stop her — respecting her choice, which hurts more than begging would. Beat: the false ending.

chapters.title: The Clause
chapters.summary: Priya's POV (interlude). Priya hands Elodie a copy of the revised contract Julian fought for — her name intact, her control absolute — and the note he wrote but never sent. Beat: revelation by proxy.

chapters.title: Running the Numbers
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Back in Boston, Elodie rebuilds her solo life and finds it airless. Her assistant asks why the best planner in the city looks like she left something on an island. Beat: success revealed as the smaller life.

chapters.title: Power Play
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian dissolves the merger entirely, walking away from the empire he spent twenty years building, and buys a stake in the Harrow inn instead. Beat: power renounced for belonging.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. On the final sailing day, Elodie boards the ferry — not fleeing this time, but going toward. She finds Julian on the dock with two tickets and no speech prepared. Beat: climax; both choose simultaneously.

chapters.title: A Harbor for the Postcard
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They miss the ferry on purpose and let the season close around them. In the empty inn, they plan nothing for anyone else — just a future, unwritten, theirs. Beat: stillness after the storm.

chapters.title: Epilogue: First Crossing
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, one year later. Spring's first ferry brings new guests to the inn Elodie and Julian run together; a nervous couple asks them to plan a small wedding. Elodie says yes, and means it. Beat: belief restored, arc closed.
